Freestyle: The Complete Guide.howTo: Swim easy freestyle with a long, relaxed stroke. Exhale slowly underwater; rotate the head to breathe rather than lifting it.
Freestyle: The Complete Guide.skills: Body position, breathing rhythm, stroke feel

Learn to Swim Freestyle: Drill Progressi.howTo: Step-by-step progression that builds freestyle from body position to full stroke. Do each stage before combining.

Catch-Up Drill.howTo: Keep one arm extended and don't start the next stroke until the other hand returns and taps it.

Fingertip Drag Drill.howTo: Drag the fingertips along the surface during recovery, keeping a high elbow, until the arm is nearly extended before the catch.

Why Sculling Drills Matter.howTo: Keep the arms underwater and scull—move hands out and in with fingers pitched—to feel water pressure and build an early catch.
Why Sculling Drills Matter.skills: Feel for water, catch, hand pitch

3 Drills to Improve Your Freestyle Catch.howTo: Sculling and early-vertical-forearm drills that set the hand and forearm as a paddle early in the pull.

Try This Drill to Improve Your Freestyle.howTo: A focused single-drill progression that cleans up alignment and stroke length.

Make Your Freestyle More Efficient.howTo: Drill that reduces drag and encourages a longer stroke. Count strokes per length and hold the count.

Boost Your Freestyle Power.howTo: Skill work that increases propulsive power in the pull through a stronger, better-connected catch.

Freestyle Evolution Drill Progression.howTo: A layered drill sequence that builds muscle memory for a faster freestyle. Master each stage, then combine.

Freestyle Kick: Flutter Kick the Right W.howTo: Kick from the hips with relaxed ankles and pointed toes; keep it small and steady. Board or on-back streamline.
Freestyle Kick: Flutter Kick the Right W.skills: Kick propulsion, ankle flexibility, leg endurance

Backstroke: The Complete Guide.howTo: Swim easy backstroke lying flat, hips high, eyes up. Steady flutter kick and a long reach behind the head.

Fix Your Backstroke By Doing This Drill.howTo: Entry-position drill: set the hand entry (pinky first) and pause to find a strong catch before pulling.

Three Drills for a Balanced Backstroke.howTo: Modified fist drill: swim 3 cycles with closed fists, then 3 with open hands to feel the catch.
Three Drills for a Balanced Backstroke.skills: Feel for the water, balance, rotation

Backstroke 6-Kick Switch.howTo: Kick on your side in streamline for 6 kicks, then take one stroke to switch sides—exaggerate the rotation.

Backstroke 6-Kick Switch (demo).howTo: Video demo of the 6-kick switch drill emphasizing shoulder rotation and a steady kick.

Try This Drill to Fix Your Backstroke.howTo: Timing drill that corrects shoulder and body rotation so arms and hips work together.

Tips and Drills to Improve Your Backstro.howTo: A five-drill sequence assembling body line, kick, rotation, and pull into full stroke.

Four Drills to Perfect Your Backstroke (.howTo: Olympian Matt Grevers' four favorite backstroke drills for elite alignment, catch, and power.

Breaststroke: The Complete Guide.howTo: Swim easy breaststroke with pull-breathe-kick-glide rhythm. Hold a streamlined glide after each kick.

Breaststroke Simple Drill Progression.howTo: Finger-count progression (0-5): from closed fist to all fingers extended, feeling how each adds catch power.
Breaststroke Simple Drill Progression.skills: Feel for the water, catch power, timing

Three Drills to Improve Breaststroke Tim.howTo: Breaststroke with a flutter kick to work hand speed and lift the trunk during the in-sweep while holding timing.

Breaststroke Body Position Drills.howTo: Breaststroke arms with a flutter kick to reduce up-and-down motion and keep hips level at the surface.
Breaststroke Body Position Drills.skills: Body position, reduced drag, flat hips

Breaststroke Pull Drills (3-pull/1-kick).howTo: Three-pull, one-kick: emphasize the pull in isolation, then apply one great pull inside normal timing.

Try These Drills to Master Breaststroke.howTo: A set of drills that build a complete, legal, efficient breaststroke from pull to kick to timing.

Breaststroke Kick Drills.howTo: Isolate the kick (board or on back) to build a strong, symmetric whip kick with quick heel recovery.

Butterfly: The Complete Guide.howTo: Press the chest, let the hips rise, two kicks per arm cycle. Keep energy forward, not up and down.

Butterfly Made Easy.howTo: Break fly into low-fatigue pieces—body dolphin and one-arm fly—to learn timing without exhaustion.

The One-Two-One Butterfly Drill.howTo: One-two-one (double-right, double-left): breathe only on the double-arm strokes to build timing without full-fly fatigue.

Tips and Drills to Improve Your Butterfl.howTo: Drills to smooth the undulation and transition to a low recovery, reducing amplitude and saving energy.

Fix Your Butterfly and Breaststroke.howTo: A shared drill that cleans up the timing and undulation common to butterfly and breaststroke.

Dryland Exercises for Butterfly.howTo: Land-based core and shoulder exercises that build the strength and mobility butterfly demands.

Kick Drills for All.howTo: A menu of kick drills (board, streamline-on-back, vertical) for every stroke and level.
Kick Drills for All.skills: Kick strength, ankle flexibility, body line

How to Perfect Your Swimming Streamline.howTo: Fingers stacked, biceps behind the head, core tight, body straight, toes pointed. Hold it off every wall.

Underwater Kick: The Complete Guide.howTo: Dolphin kick from the core in tight streamline off each wall; small fast kicks until momentum slows.

How to Write a Swimming Workout.howTo: Cool down with easy, gentle swimming to flush the muscles and lower the heart rate. Mix strokes and relax.
How to Write a Swimming Workout.skills: Recovery, aerobic flush, technique under fatigue

USMS Workout Library.howTo: Searchable library of coach-written workouts—an easy cool-down reference and source of extra sets.
